title: Module 1 · Labor & Delivery
intro: Severe blood pressure, magnesium, oxytocin, postpartum hemorrhage, GBS, intraamniotic infection, steroids, tocolysis, Rh, aspirin, induction, diabetes, and pregnancy and breastfeeding safety.

cases.title: Is this blood pressure an emergency?
cases.stem: A nurse calls: "My patient at 35 weeks has a BP of 164/104, repeated 15 minutes later at 166/106. The resident wants to know if we need to treat now."

steps.q: What makes BP in pregnancy "severe range" and urgent to treat?

options.t: Systolic 160 or more OR diastolic 110 or more, persisting 15 minutes
options.why: ACOG CO 767: either number, confirmed 15 minutes apart, defines severe range and starts the treatment clock.

options.t: Systolic 160 or more AND diastolic 110 or more, persisting 15 minutes
options.why: "And" is the trap: requiring both numbers misses most severe range patients. ACOG uses either one.

options.t: Systolic 140 or more OR diastolic 90 or more, on two readings 4 hours apart
options.why: 140/90 on two readings 4 hours apart is the definition of gestational hypertension (PB 222), not the urgent treatment threshold.

options.t: Systolic 180 or more OR diastolic 120 or more, persisting 15 minutes
options.why: 180/120 is the nonpregnant hypertensive emergency threshold. Pregnancy treats lower, at 160/110.

steps.teach: Severe range BP raises stroke risk for the mother. That is why the clock matters.
steps.where: Vital signs flowsheet in the chart. Ask the nurse for the exact times of both readings.

steps.q: How fast should treatment start once severe range BP is confirmed?

options.t: Within 30 to 60 minutes of confirmation
options.why: ACOG CO 767: treat as soon as possible, within 30 to 60 minutes, to lower stroke risk.

options.t: Within 10 minutes, before a repeat reading
options.why: 10 minutes is the labetalol recheck interval, not the treatment start window; severe range must persist 15 minutes first.

options.t: Within 2 hours, after labs return
options.why: Labs (platelets, LFTs, creatinine) guide the preeclampsia workup but never delay severe BP treatment.

options.t: Within 4 hours, once delivery is planned
options.why: 4 hours is the interval between the two readings that diagnose gestational hypertension, not a treatment window.

steps.q: Which three drugs are first line for acute severe hypertension in pregnancy?

options.t: IV labetalol
options.why: First line (ACOG CO 767).

options.t: IV hydralazine
options.why: First line (ACOG CO 767).

options.t: Immediate release oral nifedipine
options.why: First line, and the go to option without IV access (ACOG CO 767).

options.t: Oral methyldopa
options.why: Methyldopa is an option for chronic hypertension in pregnancy, but too slow for acute severe range BP.

options.t: Extended release oral nifedipine
options.why: ER nifedipine is for chronic or postpartum maintenance; the acute algorithm uses immediate release.

cases.call: **S:** Pharmacist calling about [patient] in L&D. **B:** 35 weeks, BP 164/104 then 166/106 fifteen minutes apart. **A:** That is persistent severe range BP, which ACOG says to treat within 30 to 60 minutes. **R:** I recommend labetalol 20 mg IV over 2 minutes now with a BP check in 10 minutes, unless she has asthma or heart block, in which case hydralazine or immediate release nifedipine.
cases.pearl: **160 OR 110, for 15 minutes, treat within 60.**

sources.t: ACOG Committee Opinion 767: Emergent therapy for acute onset, severe hypertension during pregnancy and the postpartum period. Obstet Gynecol 2019
ACOG Practice Bulletin 222: Gestational hypertension and preeclampsia. Obstet Gynecol 2020;135:e237-e260

cases.title: Labetalol step by step
cases.stem: Labetalol 20 mg IV was given 10 minutes ago. BP now 162/108. No asthma, heart rate 88.

steps.q: What is the next labetalol step?

options.t: Labetalol 40 mg IV over 2 minutes, recheck in 10 minutes
options.why: ACOG algorithm: 20, then 40, then 80 mg, each with a 10 minute recheck.

options.t: Labetalol 20 mg IV over 2 minutes, recheck in 10 minutes
options.why: Repeating 20 mg is a nonescalating pattern; the algorithm doubles to 40 mg when BP stays severe.

options.t: Labetalol 80 mg IV over 2 minutes, recheck in 10 minutes
options.why: 80 mg is the third step, after 40 mg fails. Skipping steps raises overshoot risk.

options.t: Labetalol 40 mg IV over 2 minutes, recheck in 20 minutes
options.why: 20 minutes is the recheck time for hydralazine and nifedipine, which act more slowly. Labetalol is rechecked at 10.

steps.teach: Why 10 minutes: IV labetalol blocks alpha 1 and beta receptors quickly (onset about 2 to 5 minutes), so you know by 10 minutes if a dose worked.

steps.q: After 40 mg the BP is still 160/106. Then 80 mg is given, and 10 minutes later BP is 161/104. What now?

options.t: Switch to hydralazine 10 mg IV and get urgent consultation
options.why: After labetalol 20, 40 and 80 mg fail, ACOG switches drug class (hydralazine 10 mg) and calls for MFM, anesthesia or critical care help.

options.t: Give labetalol 80 mg IV again and recheck in 10 minutes
options.why: Repeat 80 mg doses (up to a 300 mg cumulative label cap) are used outside obstetrics; the ACOG algorithm switches class after 80 mg.

options.t: Start a labetalol infusion at 1 to 2 mg/min
options.why: A labetalol infusion is an option only with consultation and ICU level care, not the next algorithm step on L&D.

options.t: Give nifedipine extended release 30 mg orally
options.why: ER nifedipine is a maintenance drug; the acute algorithm uses immediate release and only when labetalol or hydralazine is not working.

steps.teach: If two drug classes fail, ACOG advises urgent consultation with maternal fetal medicine, internal medicine, anesthesia or critical care.

steps.q: Which patients should NOT get labetalol?

options.t: Asthma
options.why: Beta blockade can trigger bronchospasm; start with hydralazine or nifedipine.

options.t: Heart block or heart rate below 60
options.why: Labetalol slows conduction further.

options.t: Decompensated heart failure
options.why: Beta blockade worsens acute heart failure.

options.t: Maternal heart rate above 110
options.why: The opposite: with HR above 110, labetalol is preferred because it slows the heart (CMQCC algorithm).

options.t: Gestational diabetes
options.why: Not a contraindication. Labetalol can mask hypoglycemia symptoms, so counsel, but it is still used.

cases.monitor: BP every 10 minutes during dosing, maternal heart rate, fetal heart rate tracing (neonatal bradycardia is possible).
cases.pearl: **Labetalol: 20, 40, 80, check every 10. Still high, switch to hydralazine.**
cases.alternatives: Asthma, heart block or heart failure: use hydralazine or immediate release nifedipine.

sources.t: ACOG Committee Opinion 767: Emergent therapy for acute onset, severe hypertension during pregnancy and the postpartum period. Obstet Gynecol 2019
St. Mary's L&D order sets and policies (verify locally)

workup.calc: Labetalol so far: 20 + 40 + 80 = **140 mg** in about 30 minutes, BP still severe: switch class (hydralazine 10 mg IV) rather than giving more labetalol. The injection label caps cumulative repeated doses at 300 mg ⚠️.

cases.title: Hydralazine timing
cases.stem: A patient with asthma has BP 168/110. The team chooses IV hydralazine.

steps.q: What is the starting dose and when do you recheck BP?

options.t: 5 to 10 mg IV over 2 minutes, recheck in 20 minutes
options.why: ACOG CO 767. Hydralazine peaks in 10 to 20 minutes.

options.t: 5 to 10 mg IV over 2 minutes, recheck in 10 minutes
options.why: 10 minutes is the labetalol recheck; hydralazine has not peaked yet, so you risk stacking doses.

options.t: 20 mg IV over 2 minutes, recheck in 20 minutes
options.why: 20 mg is above the ACOG starting dose and raises overshoot risk (fetal heart rate changes).

options.t: 10 to 20 mg IV over 2 minutes, recheck in 20 minutes
options.why: Labetalol 10 to 20 mg IV is the post thrombolysis stroke BP dose, not hydralazine for pregnancy.

steps.q: BP is still severe 20 minutes after hydralazine 10 mg. What does ACOG recommend next?

options.t: Hydralazine 10 mg IV again, then switch to labetalol if still severe
options.why: ACOG: repeat hydralazine 10 mg at 20 minutes; if still severe, labetalol 20 mg (asthma permitting) and get consultation.

options.t: Labetalol 20 mg IV now, since hydralazine failed once
options.why: Switching after a single hydralazine dose skips the second hydralazine step; and this patient has asthma.

options.t: Immediate release nifedipine 10 mg now, alongside more hydralazine
options.why: Adding a second agent while the first is still peaking stacks drops in BP and harms placental flow.

options.t: Hydralazine 20 mg IV, then recheck in 20 minutes
options.why: The second hydralazine dose in the ACOG algorithm is 10 mg, not 20 mg.

steps.q: What side effects do you warn the nurse about with hydralazine?

options.t: Overshoot hypotension and fetal heart rate changes
options.why: Too fast a drop reduces placental blood flow.

options.t: Reflex tachycardia and headache
options.why: Classic hydralazine effects; headache can mimic worsening preeclampsia.

options.t: Bronchospasm in patients with asthma
options.why: That is the labetalol warning; hydralazine is the preferred choice in asthma.

options.t: Neonatal bradycardia and hypoglycemia
options.why: Those are labetalol warnings (beta blockade crosses the placenta).

cases.pearl: **Hydralazine: check at 20 minutes, watch for a fast drop and tachycardia.**

sources.t: ACOG Committee Opinion 767: Emergent therapy for acute onset, severe hypertension during pregnancy and the postpartum period. Obstet Gynecol 2019

cases.title: No IV access
cases.stem: BP 170/112. The IV just infiltrated and a new one will take time.

steps.q: Which first line option needs no IV?

options.t: Immediate release nifedipine 10 mg PO
options.why: ACOG first line oral option without IV access.

options.t: Extended release nifedipine 30 mg PO
options.why: ER is for chronic or postpartum maintenance; onset is too slow for acute severe BP.

options.t: Hydralazine 10 mg PO
options.why: Oral hydralazine is a slow chronic agent; ACOG's acute hydralazine doses are IV (or IM).

options.t: Labetalol 200 mg PO
options.why: Oral labetalol is a maintenance dose for chronic hypertension, not the acute algorithm.

steps.q: When do you recheck BP after the oral dose, and what is the next dose?

options.t: Recheck in 20 minutes; if still severe, 20 mg, then 20 mg again
options.why: ACOG: 10, 20, 20 mg with 20 minute rechecks, then switch to labetalol.

options.t: Recheck in 10 minutes; if still severe, 20 mg, then 40 mg
options.why: 10 minute rechecks and doubling doses describe IV labetalol, not oral nifedipine.

options.t: Recheck in 20 minutes; if still severe, 10 mg every 20 minutes
options.why: The nifedipine algorithm escalates to 20 mg after the first 10 mg dose.

options.t: Recheck in 60 minutes; if still severe, 30 mg ER
options.why: ER nifedipine is maintenance; waiting 60 minutes breaks the 30 to 60 minute treatment goal.

steps.q: She is also on magnesium sulfate. What does the magnesium label warn about?

options.t: Label warns against it; ACOG still combines them with close monitoring
options.why: Label: avoid with calcium channel blockers; ACOG CO 767 uses the combination for severe BP with BP, reflex and breathing checks.

options.t: Absolutely contraindicated; stop magnesium before giving nifedipine
options.why: Seizure prevention is not traded away for a BP drug.

options.t: No interaction, because the two drugs act on different receptors
options.why: Both reduce calcium entry: additive hypotension and neuromuscular effects.

options.t: Halve the magnesium dose whenever nifedipine is also given
options.why: Magnesium is reduced for kidney impairment (1 g/h), not for nifedipine.

cases.pearl: **Nifedipine IR: swallow it, check at 20.** Never under the tongue.

sources.t: ACOG Committee Opinion 767: Emergent therapy for acute onset, severe hypertension during pregnancy and the postpartum period. Obstet Gynecol 2019
FDA label, Magnesium Sulfate in 5% Dextrose Injection (Hospira, 2019)

workup.calc: Nifedipine IR 10 mg PO, recheck 20 min, then 20 mg, recheck 20 min, then 20 mg; she is on magnesium, so watch BP and reflexes closely.

cases.title: Home lisinopril at 30 weeks
cases.stem: A 30 week pregnant patient with chronic hypertension lists home lisinopril 20 mg daily. She did not know she was pregnant until 14 weeks.

steps.q: What is the problem?

options.t: ACE inhibitors are contraindicated in pregnancy (fetal kidney injury)
options.why: Stop and switch; ACE inhibitors and ARBs cause fetal renal damage and low amniotic fluid.

options.t: Lisinopril is fine in pregnancy but must be lowered to 10 mg
options.why: No dose of an ACE inhibitor is acceptable in pregnancy.

options.t: Lisinopril is fine until 34 weeks, then switch
options.why: Fetal kidney injury comes from second and third trimester exposure, so stopping later is worse.

options.t: Only ARBs are contraindicated; ACE inhibitors are allowed
options.why: Both ACE inhibitors and ARBs are contraindicated in pregnancy.

steps.q: Which oral agents are preferred for chronic hypertension in pregnancy?

options.t: Labetalol
options.why: Preferred oral agent (ACC 2026; ACOG).

options.t: Nifedipine extended release
options.why: Preferred oral agent.

options.t: Methyldopa
options.why: Long track record in pregnancy; less used now because of sedation.

options.t: Atenolol
options.why: Atenolol is linked to fetal growth restriction; not preferred.

options.t: Enalapril
options.why: Enalapril is preferred only after delivery (breastfeeding), never during pregnancy.

steps.q: What else do you do?

options.t: Tell OB about the exposure so they can check amniotic fluid
options.why: Fetal kidney injury shows up as low amniotic fluid and growth problems; ultrasound review is the follow up.

options.t: Check maternal potassium and creatinine, then stop
options.why: Reasonable for ACE inhibitors in general, but the pregnancy issue is the fetus.

options.t: Plan to restart lisinopril after delivery for breastfeeding
options.why: Enalapril or captopril are the studied ACE inhibitors in breastfeeding.

options.t: File a near miss report; no clinical follow up needed
options.why: Weeks of exposure is a real exposure needing clinical follow up.

cases.call: **S/B:** 30 weeks, chronic hypertension, home lisinopril 20 mg. **A:** ACE inhibitors are contraindicated in pregnancy. **R:** Stop lisinopril and start labetalol or nifedipine ER; please let the OB team know about the exposure so they can check amniotic fluid.
cases.pearl: **No "prils" or "sartans" in pregnancy.** Labetalol or nifedipine ER instead.

sources.t: ACC: Antihypertensive medications in pregnancy and lactation (2026)
Pregnancy and Lactation page (residency Drug Hub)

cases.title: Postpartum severe BP while breastfeeding
cases.stem: Day 2 after delivery, BP 162/100 twice, 15 minutes apart. She is breastfeeding.

steps.q: Do the severe range rules still apply after delivery?

options.t: Yes: 160 or 110 for 15 minutes still means treat within 30 to 60 minutes
options.why: ACOG CO 767 applies postpartum; postpartum stroke and eclampsia are real risks.

options.t: No: postpartum severe range BP can wait until the 1 week visit
options.why: The 1 week (or 72 hour) visit is for BP checks in hypertensive patients, not for treating severe range BP.

options.t: Yes, but the threshold rises to 180/120 after delivery
options.why: 180/120 is the nonpregnant emergency threshold; postpartum stays at 160/110.

options.t: No: only treat if she also has a headache or vision change
options.why: Symptoms add concern but are not required; numbers alone qualify.

steps.q: For ongoing oral treatment while breastfeeding, which agents are preferred?

options.t: Labetalol
options.why: Compatible with breastfeeding (ACC; LactMed).

options.t: Nifedipine ER
options.why: Compatible with breastfeeding.

options.t: Enalapril
options.why: Preferred ACE inhibitor in breastfeeding; the pregnancy ban ends at delivery.

options.t: Atenolol
options.why: Atenolol concentrates in milk and has caused infant bradycardia; not preferred.

options.t: Lisinopril
options.why: Less infant data than enalapril or captopril; not the studied first choice.

steps.teach: The pregnancy rule (no ACE inhibitors) ends at delivery. Breastfeeding has its own list.

cases.pearl: **Postpartum: same severe BP rules. Breastfeeding: labetalol, nifedipine ER, enalapril.**

sources.t: ACOG Committee Opinion 767: Emergent therapy for acute onset, severe hypertension during pregnancy and the postpartum period. Obstet Gynecol 2019
ACC: Antihypertensive medications in pregnancy and lactation (2026)

cases.title: Verifying the magnesium order
cases.stem: Order: magnesium sulfate 6 g IV over 20 minutes, then 2 g/h. Patient 32 weeks, preeclampsia with severe features, SCr 0.7, urine output 60 mL/h, reflexes 2+.

steps.q: What is magnesium for here?

options.t: Prevent eclamptic seizures
options.why: Magnesium is seizure prophylaxis in preeclampsia with severe features.

options.t: Lower blood pressure
options.why: Magnesium is not an antihypertensive; severe BP still needs labetalol, hydralazine or nifedipine.

options.t: Stop preterm contractions (tocolysis)
options.why: Magnesium was used as a tocolytic, but at 32 weeks with severe preeclampsia the indication is seizure prevention.

options.t: Fetal neuroprotection
options.why: Neuroprotection is a separate indication for anticipated delivery before 32 weeks; she is 32 weeks with severe features.

steps.q: Is the dose right?

options.t: Yes: load 4 to 6 g, then 1 to 2 g/h
options.why: Label and ACOG PB 222.

options.t: No: the load should be 2 to 4 g
options.why: 2 to 4 g is the extra dose for a seizure that occurs while already on magnesium.

options.t: No: maintenance should be 1 g/h because of the 6 g load
options.why: 1 g/h is the renal impairment maintenance in the label; her kidneys are normal.

options.t: No: the load should be 10 g
options.why: 10 g (5 g each buttock) is the IM regimen when there is no IV access.

steps.q: Which safety checks do you make before verifying?

options.t: Premixed bag on a dedicated pump channel
options.why: ISMP high alert safeguards.

options.t: Load and maintenance programmed separately, with an independent double check
options.why: Prevents the whole bag running at the bolus rate.

options.t: Calcium gluconate 1 g at the bedside
options.why: The antidote must be ready before the drip starts.

options.t: Infuse through the same channel as oxytocin to save a pump
options.why: Oxytocin and magnesium must be kept apart; mix ups between them are a known L&D error.

options.t: Calcium chloride 1 g at the bedside instead of gluconate
options.why: Calcium chloride is a code and central line drug; obstetric magnesium toxicity protocols use calcium gluconate 1 g peripherally.

steps.q: How long does magnesium usually continue?

options.t: For 24 hours after delivery or the last seizure
options.why: ACOG PB 222.

options.t: For 12 hours after delivery or the last seizure
options.why: 12 hours is the maximum of the fetal neuroprotection protocol.

options.t: Until delivery, then stop in the delivery room
options.why: Eclampsia risk continues postpartum.

options.t: For 5 to 7 days, then reassess the need
options.why: 5 to 7 days is the label warning limit, not a target.

cases.monitor: Deep tendon reflexes, respiratory rate, urine output (at least 100 mL per 4 hours), mental status, oxygen saturation; magnesium levels if kidney function is impaired or toxicity is suspected.
cases.pearl: **4 to 6 load, 1 to 2 an hour, 24 hours after delivery. Calcium at the bedside.**

sources.t: ACOG Practice Bulletin 222: Gestational hypertension and preeclampsia. Obstet Gynecol 2020;135:e237-e260
FDA label, Magnesium Sulfate in 5% Dextrose Injection (Hospira, 2019)
ISMP: High alert medications in acute care settings (TXA added 2024)

workup.calc:
Order: 6 g over 20 min, then 2 g/h. **Approved?** Yes: load 4 to 6 g, maintenance 1 to 2 g/h ✅✅. **Weight based?** No, fixed grams.
With a 40 mg/mL bag: load 150 mL at 450 mL/h for 20 min; maintenance 50 mL/h.
**Kidneys:** SCr 0.7, urine 60 mL/h (240 mL per 4 h, above the 100 mL per 4 h goal) so full maintenance is reasonable.
**Reflexes 2+:** normal baseline to compare against.
**Rate:** 6 g over 20 min = 300 mg/min, the accepted obstetric exception to the 150 mg/min general limit.
whatif: Urine output 15 mL/h?
Give the load, then lower or hold maintenance (label 1 g/h in oliguria), level in a few hours, hourly reflexes and breathing, call OB now.
She also needs nifedipine for BP?
Allowed by ACOG with close BP and reflex monitoring; the label warns about the combination.
She has myasthenia gravis?
Do not give magnesium; work with OB and neurology on an alternative such as levetiracetam or a benzodiazepine.
IV infiltrates mid load?
Restart IV; if delayed, IM 5 g each buttock.

cases.title: Reflexes gone, breathing slow
cases.stem: On magnesium 2 g/h. Nurse: "Reflexes are absent, respiratory rate 11, she is drowsy, urine output 15 mL/h for 2 hours."

steps.q: What is happening?

options.t: Magnesium toxicity, made worse by low urine output
options.why: Absent reflexes, slow breathing and drowsiness with oliguria.

options.t: Expected magnesium effect at a therapeutic level
options.why: At therapeutic levels (label 2.5 to 5 mEq/L) reflexes are still present.

options.t: A postictal state after an unwitnessed eclamptic seizure
options.why: Possible to consider, but absent reflexes plus RR 11 with oliguria point to magnesium excess.

options.t: Opioid induced respiratory depression
options.why: Opioids slow breathing but do not abolish deep tendon reflexes.

steps.q: What do you recommend first?

options.t: Stop the magnesium infusion now
options.why: First step.

options.t: Calcium gluconate 1 g IV (10 mL of 10%) over 2 to 3 minutes
options.why: Antidote (ACOG).

options.t: Support breathing and call OB and anesthesia
options.why: Airway first.

options.t: Lower the rate to 1 g/h and recheck in an hour
options.why: 1 g/h is the renal impairment starting maintenance, not a response to toxicity with RR 11.

options.t: Calcium gluconate 3 g IV over 10 minutes
options.why: 3 g is the calcium gluconate dose in massive transfusion or some hyperkalemia protocols, not the magnesium antidote dose.

steps.q: Why did reflexes disappear before breathing slowed?

options.t: Reflexes fade above about 4 mEq/L; respiratory paralysis risk near 10 mEq/L
options.why: Label: reflexes diminish above 4 and may be absent at 10, when respiratory paralysis is a hazard.

options.t: Reflexes and breathing both fail at about 10 mEq/L
options.why: Reflexes are lost first, which is why they are the early warning.

options.t: Breathing fails near 4 mEq/L; reflexes near 10 mEq/L
options.why: Reversed.

options.t: Reflexes fade only above the 2.5 to 5 mEq/L target range at 12 mEq/L
options.why: 2.5 to 5 is the target range; reflexes begin to fade just above 4.

steps.q: What labs do you want?

options.t: STAT serum magnesium and creatinine
options.why: Confirms the level and the kidney cause.

options.t: STAT ionized calcium only
options.why: Calcium is the antidote, but the magnesium level and kidney function are what you need.

options.t: Platelets and liver enzymes only
options.why: Part of the HELLP workup, not the toxicity workup.

options.t: Serum potassium only
options.why: Not the cause of these findings.

cases.call: **S:** Pharmacist calling about [patient] on magnesium. **B:** 2 g/h, reflexes absent, RR 11, urine 15 mL/h for 2 hours. **A:** This looks like magnesium toxicity from poor kidney clearance. **R:** Stop the infusion now, give calcium gluconate 1 g IV over 3 minutes, support breathing, STAT magnesium level and creatinine. When she is stable, restart only at a lower rate if seizure prophylaxis is still needed.
cases.pearl: **Reflexes go before breathing. Stop the drip, give calcium.**

sources.t: FDA label, Magnesium Sulfate in 5% Dextrose Injection (Hospira, 2019)
ACOG Practice Bulletin 222: Gestational hypertension and preeclampsia. Obstet Gynecol 2020;135:e237-e260

workup.calc: Absent reflexes + RR 11 + urine 15 mL/h for 2 h (30 mL in 2 h, well below 50 mL per 2 h): accumulation. **Antidote:** calcium gluconate 1 g = 10 mL of 10% over 2 to 3 min. Expect a level above about 7 to 10 mEq/L.
whatif: Breathing stops?
Bag mask ventilation, call anesthesia and the rapid response or code team, repeat calcium as directed.
Level comes back 5 mEq/L and reflexes return?
Restart only if seizure prophylaxis is still needed, at a lower rate, with frequent levels.

cases.title: Magnesium with poor kidneys
cases.stem: New preeclampsia patient, SCr 1.9 mg/dL, urine output 20 mL/h. Magnesium is ordered 6 g load then 2 g/h.

steps.q: What does the FDA label recommend for severe renal impairment?

options.t: Load 4 g, then 1 g/h, max 20 g per 48 h, with frequent levels
options.why: Label for severe renal impairment or oliguria.

options.t: Load 6 g, then 2 g/h, with levels every 24 hours
options.why: 6 g then 2 g/h is a normal kidney regimen (also the neuroprotection regimen); too much here.

options.t: Load 2 to 4 g, then hold maintenance until delivery
options.why: 2 to 4 g is the extra dose for a seizure on magnesium; holding all maintenance removes prophylaxis.

options.t: Load 4 g, then 1 g/h, max 30 to 40 g per 24 h
options.why: 30 to 40 g per 24 h is the general label daily maximum, not the renal limit of 20 g per 48 h.

steps.q: What target level does the label give for eclampsia?

options.t: 2.5 to 5 mEq/L (3 to 6 mg/dL)
options.why: Label target for seizure control.

options.t: 1.5 to 2.5 mEq/L (1.8 to 3 mg/dL)
options.why: That is about the normal serum magnesium range, too low for seizure prophylaxis.

options.t: 5 to 8 mEq/L (6 to 10 mg/dL)
options.why: Above 4 reflexes start to fade; this range overlaps toxicity.

options.t: 10 to 12 mEq/L (12 to 15 mg/dL)
options.why: At 10 respiratory paralysis is a hazard.

cases.pearl: **Bad kidneys: 4 g, then 1 g/h, check levels.**

sources.t: FDA label, Magnesium Sulfate in 5% Dextrose Injection (Hospira, 2019)

workup.calc: SCr 1.9 and urine 20 mL/h. **Label for severe renal impairment:** 4 g load, then 1 g/h, max 20 g per 48 h, frequent levels. With a 40 mg/mL bag: load 100 mL; maintenance 25 mL/h.
whatif: Urine output drops to 10 mL/h?
Hold maintenance, level now, call OB; consider an alternative anticonvulsant if renal failure is established.
Level 2.0 mEq/L at 6 hours?
Below the label target; the team may raise the rate cautiously with repeat levels.

cases.title: Seizure while on magnesium
cases.stem: A patient on magnesium 2 g/h has a seizure.

steps.q: What is the next magnesium step?

options.t: Extra 2 to 4 g IV over 5 minutes
options.why: ACOG PB 222 for a seizure on magnesium.

options.t: A new 4 to 6 g load over 20 minutes
options.why: 4 to 6 g over 15 to 30 minutes is the initial load, not the rescue dose, and 20 minutes is too slow during a seizure.

options.t: Lorazepam 2 to 4 mg IV instead of more magnesium
options.why: Lorazepam is the ACOG checklist option when magnesium fails or cannot be used, not the first step here.

options.t: Increase maintenance to 3 g/h
options.why: 3 g/h exceeds the 1 to 2 g/h maintenance range and does not treat the active seizure.

steps.q: What else do you think about?

options.t: Protect the airway, treat severe BP, check for toxicity
options.why: Treat the whole patient.

options.t: Load phenytoin 15 to 20 mg/kg as the next routine step
options.why: An ACOG checklist alternative only when magnesium fails or cannot be used.

options.t: Prepare for an emergency cesarean during the seizure
options.why: Stabilize first; delivery planning follows.

options.t: Stop the magnesium because it did not prevent the seizure
options.why: Magnesium remains the best agent: give the extra dose and continue.

cases.pearl: **Seizure on magnesium: 2 to 4 g more over 5 minutes.**

sources.t: ACOG Practice Bulletin 222: Gestational hypertension and preeclampsia. Obstet Gynecol 2020;135:e237-e260

workup.calc: Seizure on 2 g/h: extra **2 to 4 g IV over 5 minutes** (400 to 800 mg/min, the eclampsia exception). With 40 mg/mL: 50 to 100 mL over 5 minutes (600 to 1,200 mL/h). Check reflexes and level before more.
whatif: Still seizing after the extra magnesium?
Lorazepam 2 to 4 mg IV (ACOG checklist), airway support, check level.

cases.title: Magnesium and myasthenia gravis
cases.stem: A patient with preeclampsia with severe features has myasthenia gravis on pyridostigmine.

steps.q: Why is magnesium dangerous here?

options.t: It blocks neuromuscular transmission and can trigger crisis
